sources_considered.why: Large original audit of references in actual scientific literature, available before the evaluation date.
Methods and results clarify that hallucinations are estimated as excess unmatched references above a baseline, rather than individually proven AI-caused errors.
Original evaluation of a scientific literature agent provides countervailing evidence about factuality under a designed workflow.
Read the NeurIPS citation analysis. Its selected citation cases do not establish the denominator of AI-assisted papers or the validity of their central findings.
Read the controlled citation-generation study. Raw generated literature reviews do not measure error prevalence in completed, verified scientific work.

evidence_items.locator: Abstract; methods clarified in the linked PDF, Results
evidence_items.explanation: The audit supports widespread contamination of scientific references and an association with LLM adoption. It does not supply the share of AI-assisted scientific work whose substantive findings are wrong, and its attribution is statistical.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv / Michael D. Skarlinski and colleagues
evidence_items.explanation: This evaluation shows that a designed LLM workflow can produce comparatively accurate scientific summaries. It limits an inference from hallucination risk to unavoidable failure in finished scientific work, without establishing a population-wide error rate.

unresolved_gaps: No representative denominator of scientific work produced with LLM assistance.
No established fraction of that work with material errors caused by hallucinations.
Citation-level defects are not equivalent to false scientific conclusions.
The effects of human checking and specialized retrieval workflows remain insufficiently measured at the population level.
